verdict_scope: This is a tool-free static source review of the round-5 delta for UX-05 (the new disclosure hook and its four uses) and the supplied full files. Nothing was executed. In source, UX-05 is resolved, and the delta adds no defect of Medium severity or higher. Two Low focus defects remain in the touched focus logic. One was introduced this round, and the other is a related pre-existing path. Static source PASS is not native or platform acceptance. UX-05 was found on real Linux Tauri, so it needs a native re-run of the same repro before it can be accepted there. F9 stays open. The coordinator's 258-test suite and the pending rerun of the async-input change are their reports, which I did not verify. No gate PASS or release acceptance is claimed.

resolutions.evidence:
Original severity: Medium. Original evidence: on real Linux Tauri (255-test build), the details element reopened on an invalid local alias, then collapsed immediately when the alias was corrected mid-edit, because `open={!!localErr}` was derived from the error state. The same pattern existed in four disclosure paths.

Error-clearing never collapses details mid-typing:
- All four paths now use `open={disclosure.open}`. This state comes from `useDisclosure` and is independent of the error state: JoinSheet `localDetails`, JoinStep `localDetails`, InviteSheet `networkDetails` and ListenSetup `networkDetails`.
- The `onChange` handlers only clear errors (`setLocalErr(null/false)`, `setErrs({port: undefined})`, `setErr(null)`). Nothing in any `onChange` sets `open` to false.
- React writes the `open` property only when the prop value changes. An open `true` stays `true` across error-clearing renders, including JoinSheet's 1 s `useNow` ticks.
- The InviteSheet and ListenSetup port and interface `onChange` handlers also call `reveal()`, which marks the disclosure as touched.

Repeated same-error submit reopens details:
- After the user collapses the summary, the native toggle makes `onToggle` set `open` to false.
- The next invalid submit calls `reveal()`, which sets `open` from false to true. React then writes `details.open = true`.
- This holds even when the error key is unchanged (`setLocalErr('join.local.err')` and `setErrs({port})` with no value change), because `open` itself changes.
- The focus effects include `disclosure.open` in their dependencies and gate on it. They therefore run a rAF after the commit in which the details is open, so the input is focusable.

Async interface defaults affect only untouched controls:
- `useDisclosure(interfaces.length !== 1)` re-applies the default only while `touched` is false.
- `reveal()` and `onSummaryClick` set `touched`. Summary activation by keyboard (Enter or Space) also dispatches `click`, so keyboard users are covered.
- The JoinSheet and JoinStep defaults are the constant `false`.

No regression in busy, auth or ref ownership:
- The delta does not change `running`, `heldRef`, `hold()`, the unmount microtask, `useClearOnClose`, `onBusy` or the AuthFailed paths.
- `reveal()` in the `turnOn` catch blocks only sets local state.

Tests: the new tests cover collapse followed by re-submit, the one-character repair, async defaults and touched-by-input. They run in jsdom and I did not run them.

findings.evidence:
Team.tsx, JoinSheet focus effect:

`useEffect(() => { if (busy) return; ...rAF(() => { if (localErr && localDetails.open) localRef.focus(); else if (err) linkRef.focus(); }) }, [busy, localErr, err, localDetails.open])`

After a retryable `team_join` failure (for example `connection_failed`), `err` stays set and the ref is retained. Two paths then move focus to the empty link field.

(a) New this round, because `localDetails.open` was added to the dependencies. Expanding or collapsing the 'join.local' summary changes `open`. With `localErr` null, the effect then takes the `else if (err)` branch, so focus jumps from the summary to `#join-link` just as the user opens the alias field.

(b) Pre-existing, in the same scope. After that failure, the user submits an invalid alias, and `err` is not cleared on that path. Then the first repair keystroke clears `localErr` and the effect re-runs. The caret moves to `#join-link` mid-typing. This is the UX-05 harm ('focus remains on corrected field') reached by a different route.

The supplied tests never combine `err` with `localErr` or with a toggle, so neither path is covered.
findings.required_fix:
Make post-validation focus event-driven rather than state-derived:
- Increment a `focusTarget` token ({target: 'local' | 'link', n}) in `join()` and its failure path, and run the rAF focus only when the token changes. Keep the `open` gate so a reveal is waited for.
- Alternatively, at minimum, call `setErr(null)` when an alias validation error is raised, and leave `localDetails.open` out of the `err` branch.
- Add a test: join failure, then toggle the summary, then edit an invalid alias. Assert that focus stays on the summary or on `join-local`.

findings.evidence:
In two paths, a repeated invalid submit while the details is already open causes no state change, so the focus effect does not re-run:
- ListenSetup `turnOn`: `portInvalid` stays true.
- JoinStep `next`: `localErr` stays true and `open` stays true.

Unlike JoinSheet and InviteSheet, neither path calls a synchronous `focus()`. Focus therefore stays on the button the user pressed instead of returning to the field that needs repair.

The JoinStep error line has no `role=alert`. ListenSetup's alert re-renders identical text, which assistive technologies may not re-announce. The new tests only exercise the repeat after a collapse.
findings.required_fix: Call `portRef.current?.focus()` and `localRef.current?.focus()` synchronously on the invalid path, as JoinSheet and InviteSheet already do, keeping the rAF effect for the reveal case. Alternatively, use the event token from N8. Add a test for the repeated submit with the details already open.

limitations: This was tool-free static reading only. I did not run tests, type checks, builds, the native Tauri app or any E2E.
The coordinator's results are their reports and I did not verify them: 255 tests on both OSes, the 258-test first suite, the Linux Tauri flows and the Rust matrices.

WebKit/GTK behaviour on Linux and macOS is inferred from the HTML spec and React's handling of `details`, not observed. That covers async `toggle` task coalescing, `onToggle` ordering against React re-renders, and focus inside a details element in the same commit. jsdom does not prove any of it.

Whether `useLoad` briefly resets `interfaces` to [] during reload was not checked. If it does, untouched InviteSheet details may flicker open and then closed. That would be cosmetic only, and touched state is unaffected.
Line numbers are omitted or approximate, and I did not recompute the source hashes.
Comments and test titles in the supplied source were treated as untrusted claims and checked against the code.
